entry.title: Building Hybrid Search for RAG: Combining pgvector and Full-Text Search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion
entry.summary: Most RAG tutorials show you the happy path: embed your documents, store them in a vector database, do a similarity search, done. Ship it. Then you put it in front of real users and discover that semantic search alone misses obvious keyword matches, exact product names get hallucinated into approximate nonsense, and your retrieval quality sits at maybe 60%. This post covers how we fixed it — using nothing but PostgreSQL. pgvector for semantic search, tsvector for full-text search, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion to merge the results. No Pinecone. No Elasticsearch. Just Postgres. TL;DR — Pure vector search got us ~62% retrieval precision. Adding full-text search + RRF fusion bumped it to ~84%, with near-perfect exact-match queries.
